items.title: Distinct infinite codes force the tree sets to be definably inequivalent inside Delta_5
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong; J. K. Truss
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem compares two countable weakly 2-transitive trees whose maximal chains in the one-point extensions are dense, and asserts that distinct infinite codes force the definable cardinalities of their node sets to be inequivalent, both lying in Delta_5 but not in Delta_4 (statement lines 377-379). The proof assumes an equivalence, which by the theory of definable cardinality gives a tree order on the first node set with a finite support and hence invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of that support, and then analyses that order on the pieces cut out by the support: it shows that on each piece the new order either agrees with the tree order or collapses to an antichain, using automorphisms that swap incomparable points inside the piece (proof lines 384-446). The decisive steps are the exclusion of the all-antichain case, which uses that the assumed order satisfies the same first order sentences and hence has only infinite chains, and the final recovery of the ramification orders above a point, which are first order definable and therefore equal to the codes (proof lines 448-466). H2.
